title: Frog in the Pond
statement:
There are N lily pads arranged in a straight line. The i-th lily pad contains A[i] fresh flower petals.

A frog can start from any lily pad. Whenever it lands on a lily pad, it collects all the petals present on that pad.

The frog can jump only to an adjacent lily pad (left or right) and can make at most N - 2 jumps.

Determine the maximum number of petals the frog can collect.

### Input Format
- The first line contains an integer N, the number of lily pads.
- The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the petals on each pad.

### Output Format
- Print a single integer representing the maximum number of petals the frog can collect in at most N - 2 jumps.

examples.explanation: Max jumps = 3 - 2 = 1 jump (visits 2 pads). Path: pad 2 -> pad 1. Petals = 3 + 2 = 5.
Max jumps = 4 - 2 = 2 jumps (visits 3 pads). Path: pads 2 -> 3 -> 4. Petals = 3 + 6 + 2 = 11.

constraints: The frog may start from any lily pad.
The frog may move only to adjacent lily pads.
Whenever the frog lands on a lily pad, it collects all petals on that pad.
hints: At most N - 2 jumps means the frog can visit at most (N - 2) + 1 = N - 1 contiguous lily pads.
Visiting N - 1 contiguous pads is equivalent to excluding exactly 1 lily pad from the array.
To maximize the sum of N - 1 elements, subtract the minimum element (or total_sum - min(A[i])) or max subarray of length N - 1.
discussion: Total sum minus minimum element or sliding window of length N - 1.
